context:
Goal: tests that catch real faults, in every repo.
Problem (money): a CI job for the test-strength check spends GitHub minutes on every batch, so it waits on your word.
Based on (read): the test-strength check is mutation testing: it plants small breaks in new code and counts how many the tests catch. We trust that count in two ways. (1) Known-bug replay: re-plant a real past bug (for example the undo incidents 3297d8fa and df25a68d) and the tests must catch it. (2) Equivalent breaks: a planted change that does not change behaviour can never be caught, so a miss is read by hand before it counts against a test. claude-settings' own guards run this today (mutate_guard, 487 of 487 caught on main 446f2d3d).
Based on (measured): on the last 50 merged PRs per repo, 5 deliberate breaks each: q_max's tests caught 73% (155 tried); banchi's Python tests caught 50% (52 tried); banchi's TypeScript tests caught 0 of 10.
Based on (read): your 163 note asked for a banchi fix first. It landed: banchi #1055 runs the tests for one file, and claude-settings #1243 makes the replay pick them (batch 10, main 59bff081, Nov 5 06:36 CST). banchi's catch rates above were measured before that fix; a new count is unmeasured.
Departs from: today the check runs only by hand — adds a test-strength job to CI.
holds: Any CI job for test strength.
lane: coordinator: lane mutation-ci-report (PR #1262) archived; re-ask after mutation-tests-for-imports merges (triage audit 14:45 CST)

lastAnswer.note: we also reopen this in a while after logging for a bit. Routed 07:44 CST Nov 5 to the coordinator for a lane; the re-ask after a logging period is filed on roadmap step test-practices-first-principles.

options.gain: Each batch shows its untested lines, with no risk to merges.
options.how: A CI job on each batch PR breaks its new product lines, lists each break no test caught, and never fails the run.
options.label: Report only
options.lose: About one extra job per batch, cost not yet measured; weak tests still merge.

options.how: The same job fails the batch when its tests catch fewer than a set share of breaks, for example 60% of new product lines.
options.label: Block below a floor
options.lose: GitHub minutes on every batch; a share set too high blocks good work.

options.how: No CI job; the check runs when someone asks for it.
options.label: By hand only
options.lose: Nothing watches test strength between hand runs.

options.gain: Each batch shows untested lines, and the check proves itself on past bugs.
options.how: Each batch reports untested lines, and the check re-plants known past bugs to prove it catches them.
options.label: Report only, plus known-bug replay
options.lose: One more step per batch, cost not yet measured.

ref: PRs #996, #1010, #1080 and banchi #1052; roadmap step test-practices-first-principles
reply: Your pick d is routed to the coordinator for a lane: a report-only test-strength job on each batch, plus the known-bug replay. Your follow-up is filed on roadmap step test-practices-first-principles: once the job has logged results for a while, this question comes back, with the measured catch rates, to ask whether a weak result should block. This item closes when the lane merges.
title: Should CI check test strength on each batch, and should a weak result block the merge?
why: Recommended: d. It shows weak tests on every batch without blocking merges, and the replay of past bugs shows the check itself works.
